html:
A stone arch bridge over the Xiao River in Hebei, north China, built between 595 and 605 under the Sui dynasty. It is the oldest bridge still standing in China and the oldest open-spandrel stone arch bridge in the world.

The design is credited to a craftsman named Li Chun. Instead of a heavy half circle, he used one long, flat arch of stone. Over each end of the arch he left two small arches open. These open spandrels cut the weight of the bridge and let floodwater pass through, which helped it survive more than fourteen centuries of floods, earthquakes and traffic.

Bridges of this type did not appear in Europe until centuries later. It belongs to the same burst of Sui building that produced the Grand Canal and the new capital at Chang'an.
